proposals.title: Neighborhood Composition Similarity Mapping
proposals.summary: This analysis will quantify spatial heterogeneity by comparing the transcriptomic profiles of local neighborhoods within a tissue section. Each neighborhood’s cell-state composition will be summarized and then compared using similarity scores that account for differences in neighborhood size, spatial resolution, and cell density. The method will leverage techniques such as graph-based clustering and distance metrics to identify similar local microenvironments.

proposals.title: Recurrent Microenvironment Identification
proposals.summary: In this analysis, unsupervised clustering algorithms will be applied to spatial transcriptomics data to detect recurrent microenvironments within tissues. Spatial smoothing and feature extraction will help in highlighting regions with similar patterns of gene expression. The analysis will focus on identifying recurrent combinations of cell types and states, providing insights into localized tissue architecture and pathology boundaries.

proposals.title: Differential Neighborhood Analysis Across Conditions
proposals.summary: This approach will systematically compare the local neighborhood compositions between different conditions (e.g., disease vs. healthy) within spatial omics datasets. By distinguishing true alterations in cellular interactions from those due to sampling resolution or density variations, the analysis will detect regions with significant changes in heterogeneity and organization, paving the way for identifying condition-specific microenvironment disruptions.

proposals.title: Spatial Ligand–Receptor Interaction Mapping
proposals.summary: Here, the focus is on linking spatial transcriptomic patterns to potential intercellular communication events. By overlaying ligand–receptor gene expression on spatial coordinates, the analysis will reveal hotspots of potential signaling activity. This will provide insight into how cell-cell interactions are modulated within distinct local microenvironments and how they correlate with neighboring cell compositions.

proposals.title: Multi-Scale Spatial Integration
proposals.summary: This analysis will integrate data collected at multiple spatial resolutions by normalizing for cell density and spot size variances. An algorithm will be developed to combine fine-scale and coarse-scale neighborhood profiles, capturing both localized heterogeneity and broader tissue organization. The resulting multi-scale view can help identify gradients and transitions that are not apparent at a single resolution.

proposals.title: Continuous Gradient and Boundary Detection
proposals.summary: The aim of this analysis is to identify and characterize continuous transitions in gene expression at tissue boundaries. By applying spatial gradient detection and segmentation techniques, it will delineate transition zones where localized changes in cell state compositions occur. This approach can be crucial in understanding how disease boundaries develop and evolve within a heterogeneous microenvironment.

proposals.title: Normalization of Neighborhood Composition by Cell Density
proposals.summary: This analysis will focus on correcting for the impact of variable cell densities on spatial transcriptomics measurements. A normalization framework will be developed that adjusts neighborhood composition scores based on local cell counts, ensuring that observed differences in gene expression and cellular states reflect true biological variation rather than artifacts of differential spot resolution or cell abundance.

proposals.title: Spatial Deconvolution of Mixed Cell Populations
proposals.summary: Given that many spatial transcriptomics platforms capture signals from multiple cells within a spot, this analysis will employ deconvolution techniques to resolve mixed cell-type signals into individual components. Once deconvolved, the refined spatial maps of cell type distribution will be analyzed for local heterogeneity, allowing for more accurate identification of microenvironmental niches and their specific gene expression profiles.

proposals.title: Spatial Autocorrelation of Gene Expression Patterns
proposals.summary: This analysis will quantify the degree of spatial autocorrelation in gene expression across a tissue section. Metrics like Moran’s I and Geary’s C will be computed to assess whether high or low expression values cluster together spatially. The resulting spatial statistics will help determine if particular genes or pathways exhibit coordinated expression within defined neighborhoods, supporting the identification of functionally relevant microenvironments.

proposals.title: Integration of Tissue Morphology with Spatial Transcriptomics
proposals.summary: This approach will combine high-resolution imaging or histopathological annotations with spatial transcriptomics data to contextualize gene expression patterns. By aligning molecular data with morphological boundaries, the analysis will refine the segmentation of tissue regions and highlight how gene expression gradients and neighborhood compositions vary in association with architectural features, enhancing the biological interpretability of spatial heterogeneity.
